summary.headline: H2 FY26 revenue nearly doubled to INR 125 crore (+~100% YoY) with EBITDA up 42% to INR 15.9 crore, though margin fell to 13%.
summary.overview: DSM Fresh Foods (Zappfresh) reported H2 FY26 revenue of about INR 125 crore versus INR 65 crore in H2 FY25, with EBITDA of about INR 15.9 crore (13% margin) and PBT of INR 11.5 crore. For full FY26, revenue was about INR 221 crore (+69%), EBITDA about INR 31 crore, and reported PAT INR 14.4 crore, which management says is INR 18.4 crore before a deferred tax impact. Growth was driven by B2B/HoReCa, fish and seafood, and early ramp of the Meevaa ready-to-eat range, while B2C volumes were flat to down. Management guided to 70-80% revenue growth in FY27 and a 3-4% EBITDA margin improvement over two years.

segments.name: B2B / HoReCa
segments.commentary: Contributes about 68% of FY26 revenue (about 70% per later remark) versus 20-25% in FY25; serves more than 300 restaurant and institutional customers. Gross margin about 20-25%.

segments.name: B2C (online and retail)
segments.commentary: About 32% of FY26 revenue; gross margin about 45-50%. Online-only today, with monthly transacting users down about 15% in H2 to INR 80,000-90,000 monthly transactions; retention rate about 85%.

segments.name: Category mix: chicken, mutton, fish/seafood
segments.commentary: Chicken about 50% of revenue; fish rose from 21% in H1 to 27% in H2 FY26, targeted at 30-35% in FY27. Mutton to decline; chicken guided to 40-45% in FY27.

segments.name: Meevaa Foods (frozen ready-to-eat, export and domestic)
segments.commentary: Launched recently with over 5,000 orders in 48 hours. Current annualised run rate INR 30-40 crore, about 90% export (US, Canada, Europe); guided to 15-20% of FY27 revenue (at least INR 70 crore) and about 50% gross margin. Capacity INR 500 crore at Chandigarh plant.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target of 70-80%, with Meevaa contributing 15-20% of revenue and fish and seafood rising to 30-35% of mix.

EBITDA margin expected to improve by at least 3-4 percentage points over the next two years, driven by aquaculture (200-300 bps on fish), a higher ready-to-eat share (about 50% gross margin), and a B2B/B2C split near 50-50 or 53% B2C in the medium term.
Management said the deferred tax drag will not recur in H1 FY27, with underlying PAT around INR 18 crore at standard tax rates.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive in 2-3 years after working capital investment.
Partner store network to scale from about 100 stores to 300-400 by year end; each store averages INR 5 lakh monthly revenue and 8-10% net margin.
capex_capacity: Meevaa Foods plant in Chandigarh is state-of-the-art, with capacity of INR 500 crore revenue per year on land, plant and machinery already in place.
Marina Aqua integrated aquaculture platform on about 270 acres: land parcels in Kanpur, Ghaziabad, Nagpur and Assam; around 300 seafood farmers in the FPO.
Partner store (local meat shop) model: about 100 stores onboarded across Mumbai and Bangalore, targeting 300-400 by year end; pilot of 15-20 stores.
Planned new cities include Pune, Nashik and near-Bangalore markets; management did not disclose capex per new city.
demand_pricing: Management said the mix shift toward B2B and fish reduced gross margin; B2C gross margin about 45-50% vs B2B about 20-25%.
Ready-to-eat gross margin about 50%, roughly 25-30 percentage points above quick commerce-channel products after commission and marketing costs, per management.
Meevaa targets NRI consumers in US, Canada and Europe with northern Indian gourmet snacks, avoiding frenchfries and nuggets categories where large FMCG players compete.
Management views domestic frozen competition as high; domestic strategy to add seekh kebab and tikka products through partner stores.

qa_highlights.question: Why did B2C share fall from about 48% in H1 to 32% in H2, and how does B2C work?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the mix is intended to move toward about 50-50 over time; the B2B push is to absorb volume from the new Marina Aqua farming business. B2C is currently online only, with retail stores to be added.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from H2 FY25 to H2 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly the rising B2B share (close to 70%) with lower gross margin (20-25% vs 45-50% in B2C); a slight gross margin dip was also cited.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of the 70-80% FY27 growth target?
qa_highlights.answer: Meevaa at 15-20%, fish and seafood rising from 27% to 30-35%, chicken at 40-45% and mutton declining. Meevaa run rate is INR 30-40 crore annualised, expected to deliver at least INR 70 crore in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the economics of a partner store?
qa_highlights.answer: Each store averages INR 5 lakh monthly revenue with 8-10% net margin, around INR 50,000 monthly profit per store.

qa_highlights.question: Is cash flow from operations positive, and is fundraising planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating cash flow is negative due to working capital investment; cash is INR 20-25 crore, net debt to equity is below 0.5x, and management expects positive operating cash flow in 2-3 years. Debt headroom exists, and warrant exercise by the promoter is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Are further acquisitions planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Nothing is in the immediate pipeline; focus is on the fish and seafood project, Meevaa and retail rollout.

risks_watch: Cash flow from operations is negative despite EBITDA; working capital needs rise with scale, and positive operating cash flow is not expected for 2-3 years.
B2C volumes flat to down and monthly active users down about 15% in H2; management attributes this to a shift of focus, so monitor B2C recovery and retention (85%).
Margin dilution from B2B-heavy mix; FY26 reported PAT includes a deferred tax impact that management says will not recur in H1 FY27.
Export and shipping exposure to the war, raw material pressures, and perishable inventory wastage risk (per management).
Meevaa targets depend on a young product; management calls the 15-20% FY27 contribution a sharp ramp, and the frozen category is competitive domestically.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, targets and the Meevaa and aquaculture strategy; more hesitant and evasive on specific numbers, such as net revenue by year, cash-flow timing and new-city capex, which were not quantified.
key_quotes: The margin profile will certainly improve, because, we are looking at 20% contribution coming in the new financial year, from the Meevaa range.
What gives us confidence today is that growth is no longer coming at the cost of profitability.
So, it's not that we are establishing it.
So, nothing is in immediate pipeline, because acquisitions takes a long time and, we have our hands full currently.

growth.why: Management targets 70-80% FY27 revenue growth (midpoint 75%), backed by the commissioned INR 500 crore Chandigarh Meevaa plant, Meevaa's INR 30-40 crore current run rate and partner-store scale-up from ~100 to 300-400, though no order book or contract quantification was given for the bulk of the guidance.
